# Business categories

When submitting a business profile, classify the business using `industryCategories`. Submit one or more values from the [Industry categories](#industry-categories) list below. You should map from the information you have about the business to our categories. If this is problematic, please [get in touch with us](/guides/product/partner) to discuss alternate solutions.

`industryCategories` is accepted on every create and update business profile endpoint, including the existing V2 and V3 flows. This is the classification system to use for all new integrations.

An older, deprecated hierarchy of `firstLevelCategory` and `secondLevelCategory` values is still accepted on the same endpoints. Send **either** `industryCategories` **or** the legacy pair in a request, a request containing both formats is rejected with a `400`. If you are currently sending the legacy fields, see [Migrating to industry categories](/guides/product/account-setup/customer-onboarding/migrate-business-profile-industry-categories).

Some categories cover activities Wise does not support for all partners, and are rejected unless your integration is explicitly permitted to use them. If a business falls into one of these categories, [get in touch with us](/guides/product/partner) before you go live.

## Industry categories

The categories are grouped below by industry. When submitting values, pass the category name only (for example `SOFTWARE_DEVELOPMENT_PUBLISHING`), not the group name.

## Legacy categories

The legacy categories are still accepted on the same create and update business profile endpoints as `industryCategories`, but cannot be combined with it in one request. A business is described by a single `firstLevelCategory` and a single `secondLevelCategory`, taken from the fixed hierarchy below.

`firstLevelCategory` and `secondLevelCategory` are deprecated. See [Migrating to industry categories](/guides/product/account-setup/customer-onboarding/migrate-business-profile-industry-categories).
